findings.evidence: The 223-line ensure-ci example repeatedly instructs native task tracking: "Use TodoWrite to track your progress:" and "Track progress: Use TodoWrite for every iteration", alongside generic guidance such as "Be systematic" and "Don't guess". This substantially dilutes the command-specific knowledge.
findings.fix: Condense ensure-ci to its project-specific check mapping, bounded stopping policy and concise reporting template. Remove repeated TodoWrite instructions and generic run/fix recaps; preserve all erk attribution and source credits.

findings.evidence: The release example says: "If the tag is there, report success" after a failed or timed-out push. If another publisher creates that tag for a different commit between validation and pushing, the push fails but this branch incorrectly reports success.
findings.fix: Record the intended commit before tagging. After a failed or timed-out push, query the exact remote tag and its peeled target, and report success only when the target matches the intended commit. Report a conflict for a different target, stop when the query fails or remains inconclusive, and permit retry only when a successful query proves absence.

findings.evidence: "Repeat at most <N> times" checks first and fixes afterward, then says "After <N> attempts without success, report STUCK". A successful fix on the final iteration is never checked, so the skeleton can report STUCK after actually repairing the failure.
findings.fix: Run an initial baseline check, then define each of the N attempts as a fix followed by a fresh check. Update stuck detection from those observed results, return SUCCESS immediately on a passing check, and report exhaustion only after the final verification fails.

findings.evidence: The five evals are "project-ci-command", "global-argument-command", "underspecified-workflow", "release-from-transcript" and "shell-special-argument"; none exercises the supported "Plan, approve, execute" pattern.
findings.fix: Add a multi-turn approval-gate eval asserting that drafting and feedback cause no writes, the approval wait remains in the main conversation, and explicit approval saves the plan before execution begins.
